![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/6ba207cd34725ec2e3995eb0f90e63bedc8573300335b2d31163457ef8ee9bad.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $x={y}^{2}+1$ and $x=2{y}^{2}$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=-2.$ Find the volume of the resulting solid.
question.worked_solution:
First, to determine the limits of integration, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2} & ={y}^{2}+1 \\ {y}^{2} & =1 \\ y & =-1,1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, our limits of integration are from $y=-1$ to $y=1.$

Next, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/41f8dff0676c5cf8952f46b174ff4f98deeb97eec272e417f145b4782770c156.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x=2{y}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x={y}^{2}+1.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x={y}^{2}+1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/b4d3d75dfab4aa6382bf47f06a57036ec612a05c90d0764cd48fdc1f150f2453.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}{[\,({y}^{2}+1)-(-2)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}{[{y}^{2}+3]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=2{y}^{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/6f79c95e2b2d3aaf71e6dfac5ca93fa20261f5f40e1660cefc4ac23af3e56cf8.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}{[\,(2{y}^{2})-(-2)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}{[2{y}^{2}+2]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}({[{y}^{2}+3]}^{2}-{[2{y}^{2}+2]}^{2})\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}(-3{y}^{4}-2{y}^{2}+5)\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {(-\frac{3{y}^{5}}{5}-\frac{2{y}^{3}}{3}+5y)|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\pi [(-\frac{3\cdot {1}^{5}}{5}-\frac{2\cdot {1}^{3}}{3}+5\cdot 1)-(-\frac{3\cdot (-1)^{5}}{5}-\frac{2\cdot (-1)^{3}}{3}+5\cdot (-1))] \\  & =\frac{112\pi }{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
